Mr. Khulesh Sahu, Advocate appears along with Mr. Swayam Tehanguria, Counsel for the Appellant.
Mr. Tarkeshwar Nande, Panel lawyer for the State.

Heard on admission as well as on I.A. No.
01/2024, an application under Section 430 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita of 2013 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

By virtue of the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 23.07.2024 passed in Session Trial No. 50/2016 by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Korba, District- Korba,
Chhattisgarh, appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
 Conviction Sentence  Under Section 498-A of RI for 03 year, fine of

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge, Korba, District- Korba,
Chhattisgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: the Indian Penal Rs.5,50,000/-.
In default of  Code,1860 payment further R.I. for 06  months.

Learned Counsel appearing for the appellant submits that there is 21 days delay in FIR registration,
there is absence of allegations in suicide note and witness no. 1 to 4 being relatives of the deceased,
are inherently biased and cannot be deemed reliable.
He also contended that the essential elements of Section 498A is not met and there is adverse presumption under Section 113B.
Based on these grounds it is submitted that his application (I.A. No. 01/2024) may be allowed.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State/Respondent has opposed the said application.

Abhishek Singh vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129659584/
1 Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and also looking to the judgment passed by the Trial Court, the nature of offence, age of the appellant and specially looking to the detention period of the appellant which is only 3 years and he he has already paid the fine amount,I am inclined to allow this application without commenting anything on merits of the case.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 01/2024 is allowed and it is directed that substantive jail sentence imposed upon the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and the appellant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 10,000/- with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court .

sentences.text: After being released on bail, he shall appear before the Registry of this Court on 25.09.2024 and thereafter he shall continue to appear before the Trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry on this behalf and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given by the said court till the disposal of this appeal.
In view of above, I.A. No. 01/2024 is allowed and stands disposed of.
List this case for final hearing in its due course.
Call for the records from the concerned Trial Court.
